title: B2: executor.py routes through Pool.pick_executor; per-executor -m, cooldowns via quota_group; log_run gains executor + complexity; token field normalized
spec:
Why: after B1 (T-0016) the pool knows several codex executors, but executor.py still reads pool.cfg["codex"]["model"] (executor.py:81) and cools a single Codex singleton (executor.py:55). Scouts T-0012/T-0013 mapped the call sites. Depends on B1 being merged into goal/T-0005 (this task's worktree is created from that branch).

What (≤4 files: orchestrator/executor.py, orchestrator/spawn.py, orchestrator/bus.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py):
1. executor.start(task_id, prompt): `ex = pool.pick_executor("execute", t["complexity"], scores=pool.scores())` where `Pool.scores()` returns {} if not defined yet (use getattr with a default so B3 can add it); if ex is None → existing _exhausted path. Record `bus.update(task_id, executor=ex.id, tier=ex.id)`; increment ex.running/day_tasks instead of pool.codex.*; pass `-m ex.model`. executor.reply must reuse `t["executor"]` (same thread, same model) — never re-pick mid-task.
2. executor._run: on a usage-limit error call `pool.cooldown_executor(ex.id, secs, reason)` (cools the quota_group) instead of setting pool.codex.cooldown_until; keep the legacy pool.codex fields updated too so status()["codex"] stays meaningful. bus.log_run everywhere in executor.py and spawn.py gains `executor=<id or "claude:"+tier>` and `complexity=t["complexity"]`. Normalize the Codex token key: write `cache_read_input_tokens` (from Codex's cached_input_tokens) so cli cost aggregation is uniform; keep the old key too for one release.
3. spawn.run_worker execute path (Claude fallback): bus.update(task_id, executor=f"claude:{tier}") and the same log fields.
4. tests: (a) with the TMP pool.toml, `executor.start` on a complexity-3 task uses a codex executor whose model is one of the four ids — monkeypatch `executor._run` to capture args and assert "-m" is followed by that model; (b) a fake usage-limit result (patch _run to return the held shape / or call the cooldown path directly) cools all chatgpt-group executors and `pool.codex_available()` becomes False; (c) run log line contains executor and complexity. Keep the existing Executor tests green (adapt only if they assert the singleton).

Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py`. Commit: "executor: route via pick_executor, per-executor -m and quota-group cooldowns, executor+complexity in run logs" with a revert-path body.
acceptance: uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py exits 0 with the three new executor tests
grep shows no remaining read of pool.cfg["codex"]["model"] in executor.py
a usage-limit hit on one codex executor cools every executor in its quota_group (test b)
runs jsonl entries written by executor.py and spawn.py contain executor and complexity
git diff --stat limited to orchestrator/executor.py, orchestrator/spawn.py, orchestrator/bus.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py

result.summary:
Done. Committed as `a01dc3c` on `task/T-0017`.

## Summary

- `executor.start` picks its row with `pool.pick_executor("execute", t["complexity"], scores=getattr(pool, "scores", dict)())` and passes `-m ex.model`. `ex is None` (or a non-codex provider) falls through to the existing `_exhausted` path. It records `executor=ex.id, tier=ex.id` on the bus and bumps `ex.day_tasks` / `ex.running`, with `pool.codex.*` still mirrored so `status()["codex"]` stays meaningful until B3 drops it.
- `executor.reply` reuses `t["executor"]` (falling back to `pool._legacy_executor()` for tasks created before this change) — same thread, same model, no re-pick mid-task.
- `_run` on a usage-limit error calls `pool.cooldown_executor(ex.id, secs, "codex usage limit")`, which cools every enabled member of the quota group, and still sets the legacy `pool.codex.cooldown_until`.
- All `bus.log_run` calls in `executor.py` and `spawn.py` carry `executor` and `complexity`; `tier` on Codex runs is now the executor id instead of the hardcoded `"astra"`. New `_tokens()` writes `cache_read_input_tokens` alongside Codex's `cached_input_tokens` so `cli.cost` sums one key across providers.
- `spawn.run_worker`'s execute path sets `executor="claude:<tier>"` before rendering the prompt, so the fallback run's log lines say which tier took it.

Acceptance checks: no remaining read of `pool.cfg["codex"]["model"]` in `executor.py` (the two `cfg["codex"]` hits are `dangerous_full_access` and `on_exhausted`); `git diff --stat` limited to the four scoped files.

## Files changed
`orchestrator/executor.py`, `orchestrator/spawn.py`, `orchestrator/bus.py` (docstrings for the new `update`/`log_run` fields), `tests/test_orchestrator.py`.

## Tests
`uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` — 33 tests, OK, no failures (ran twice; state is clean across runs). `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` exits 0. Three new tests in `Executor`: `test_start_routes_through_pick_executor`, `test_usage_limit_cools_the_whole_quota_group`, `test_run_log_carries_executor_and_complexity`. Existing Executor tests needed no changes.

One note: the spec said to run `scripts/tests_green.sh`, which doesn't exist in this repo — the equivalent is `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh`, which I ran.
